newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December spot natgas unchanged after holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December spot natgas unchanged after holiday.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for December were unchanged Friday due to the absence of traders and expiration of all nomination deadlines for first-of-the-month deliveries.
Most sources were awaiting the release of monthly indices before making the next move in the swing market. With such wide swings in prices, there was a lot of uncertainty on where indices would fall.
December prices in the Gulf were notionally in the mid-$3.80s, up from most bidweek levels, and up more than a $1 from November index levels.
Before traders exited for the long holiday weekend, prices at the New York city-gate were in the $4.70s and $4.80s, up about $1.50 from November's index.
Temperatures in the Northeast are expected to moderate throughout this weekend to reach near-normal levels Monday. On Tuesday, however, cooler temperatures are forecast again.
Prior to the holiday, Midcontinent prices were around $3.80 for next month, rising more than a $1 from November indices.
Forecasters are calling for mostly above-normal temperatures through the weekend in the Midwest, with cooler weather expected to follow next week in the northern plains and western Great Lakes area.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices were in low-$3.60s, up about $1.20 from November's index.

Temperatures in Texas are expected to average four to 10 degrees Fahrenheit above-normal on Saturday, but below-normal temperatures are forecast to arrive by Sunday and continue through the early part of next week.

American Gas Association reported Wednesday natural gas stocks at the week ending November 22 dropped 66 billion cubic feet (bcf) to 80 percent of capacity. In the East, stocks fell by 46 bcf to 90 percent of capacity, while in the Producing region, inventories dropped 14 bcf to 68 percent full. In the West, stocks slipped six bcf to 68 percent of capacity.
